Subject: Clarifying unitization, rounding and minimums for pilot

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks again for the demo today. Procurement had a few follow-ups after we reviewed the pricing exhibit: they want a plain-English explanation of how you (1) round token counts for streaming calls, (2) treat long-context requests that exceed the 16k window, and (3) how minimums are assessed for short bursts (we have lots of short, high-frequency assistant calls).

Specifically:
- If a streaming call produces 3,200 tokens, how is that billed (any rounding up to a quantum or per-token)?
- If a single user request requires 20k context because they include a long document, do you bill by the model's max context (16k) + an overflow, or is it segmented?
- For the pilot, can we get an illustrative invoice line for a week with 20k short calls averaging 180 tokens each vs 200 long calls at 6k tokens?

Procurement wants this in writing to walk the legal team through the math. Would you be able to send a short write-up + example lines?

Best,
Vera
Vera Hahn
Head of Platform Partnerships — BluePilot

P.S. attaching the sample telemetry CSV they referenced (we pulled it from our test environment).

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>

Hi Vera —

Thanks — this is great context. Attached is a short exhibit that walks through the billing rules and three worked examples. High level answers here and then the spreadsheet has line-item math: 

1) Rounding: streaming responses are measured per-token and then aggregated per-request. We bill tokens to the nearest token; however we apply a minimum charge quantum of 25 tokens per request for hosted API pilots to protect against very short microcalls. That means if a request consumes 3 tokens, it will be billed as 25 tokens. For typical calls (3,200 tokens) there is no additional quantum rounding beyond integer tokens.

2) Over-context handling: for requests with context > model max, we do not silently extend the context window. We either: (a) reject with a 413-like error, or (b) if you opt into automatic segmentation, we segment the user-supplied context into contiguous 16k chunks and issue N requests under the hood. In segmentation mode you are charged for each underlying request in full. For the pilot we usually recommend segmentation + prefix caching to reduce repeated charge of stable system prompts.

3) Minimums and bursts: minimums are assessed per-request (the 25-token minimum) and we also have per-account invoice minimums for pilots under $500/month (we floor monthly billed usage to $500 unless you take the pilot waiver). For high-frequency short calls we suggest enabling prefix reuse + local KV cache (dedicated) which greatly reduces billable tokens; we can also offer a temporary 60% short-call smoothing concession for the first two months of the pilot (see proposal below).

Example invoice lines (from attached exhibit):
- 20,000 short calls @ average billed tokens 180 -> 3,600,000 billable tokens -> 3,600,000 * $0.000015/token = $54.00
- 200 long calls @ 6,000 tokens -> 1,200,000 billable tokens -> 1,200,000 * $0.000015 = $18.00

Net: $72.00 for the illustrative week (before discounts). With the 60% short-call smoothing concession applied to short calls in months 1–2 the short-call line would become $21.60.

I'll paste the worked lines below and attach the PDF + CSV with the math. If procurement wants different floor or quantum assumptions, flag which numbers they need.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Marissa —

Reviewing Vera's ask and the draft exhibit. A couple of internal notes to keep in mind before we finalize the customer copy:

- The 25-token per-request minimum is something we can offer to pilots but legal prefers wording that describes it as "per-request minimum billing quantum for hosted pilot endpoints." Make sure we avoid implying it's a permanent product-wide floor.
- For segmentation: emphasize that segmentation charges are per-underlying-model-call. If BluePilot wants to avoid being charged for repeated stable system context, we should push the recommended architecture of prefix caching + session KV reuse (works well if they host Dedicated or use our dedicated prefix cache on hosted).
- Concession: a 60% smoothing concession on short-call charge is material; need an internal approval note — propose offering it for the first two months only, capped at $10k credit. If they want a longer concession we should tie it to a 6- or 12-month committed capacity.

Marissa, can you add the exact legal-friendly phrasing for the minimum and the pilot waiver line? I can help size the credit cap and draft the clause for the SOW.

Karthik
Director, Commercial Strategy

Vera / team —

Following up with the formalized note and a couple of concessions for the pilot. Summary below — the attached PDF has line-by-line math pulled from your CSV.

What we will confirm in the SOW: 
- Per-request billing: tokens billed as integers; hosted pilot per-request minimum billed quantum of 25 tokens (applies only to named hosted pilot endpoints; will be described as a pilot configuration in the SOW).
- Overflow/context > model max: segmentation is opt-in. If enabled, each 16k chunk is billed as an individual model call. We will include guidance for prefix caching to limit repeated charge on stable context.
- Monthly pilot floor: monthly invoiced usage will be floored at $500 for the pilot unless BluePilot requests a waiver in writing.

Concessions proposed for BluePilot pilot: 
1) Short-call smoothing: 60% off billable short-call tokens (requests averaging < 400 billed tokens) for months 1–2 up to a $10,000 credit cap.
2) Segmentation pilot discount: for segmented overflow calls we will apply an 20% discount on the overflow model calls for month 1 to help them model cost while they instrument prefix caching.

Next steps: if that looks OK we will: (a) have Marissa add the legal-friendly language for the minimum and waiver into the SOW, (b) Karthik will finalize the credit cap verbiage, and (c) we can get a DocuSign exhibit signed.

If procurement wants a worked invoice with their actual telemetry (the CSV you attached) we can produce a sample invoice — say yes and we'll deliver the sample within 48 hours.

Thanks —
Kimberly
